newsitem.title: USA: Delta quarterly net edges down, ValuJet posts loss.
newsitem.headline: Delta quarterly net edges down, ValuJet posts loss.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Thursday said profits fell in the latest quarter but hit a record for its fiscal year, resulting in a $145 million profit-sharing payout to employees that was the largest in its three-year programme.

Other carriers reported mixed results. ValuJet Inc., still struggling after a fatal crash last year, reported a loss of $9.2 million for the second quarter. Southwest Airlines Co. beat expectations with earnings of $94 million, up 13 percent.
The latest results come after the nation's largest airlines reported generally strong earnings while smaller ones struggled.

Delta, the nation's third-largest carrier, said profits fell to $301 million in its fourth quarter ended in June, from a record $328 million a year earlier. Earnings per share fell to $3.98 from $5.77.
Sales rose to $3.54 billion from $3.36 billion on strong passenger traffic levels and increased cargo traffic, the carrier said.

"Delta achieved nearly a 15 percent operating margin in a quarter with very tough economic comparisons with last year's outstanding June quarter, both on the revenue and the cost side," Chairman Ronald Allen said.
For fiscal 1997, net income soared 34 percent to $886 million, or $11.72 a share, from $662 million, or $11.13 a share, the previous year.

During the year, Delta, based in Atlanta, took $52 million in pretax restructuring and other charges for the realignment of its trans-Atlantic and European operations announced in January. The charges were recorded in the March quarter.

Revenue grew 9 percent to $13.59 billion from $12.46 billion. Passenger revenue grew 8 percent on a 10 percent rise in passenger traffic partly offset by a 2 percent drop in yield, a measure of profitability, it said.
Delta also said it named two executives to head the company while it searches for a permanent replacement for retiring Chairman Allen.
Delta said Maurice Worth has been named acting chief executive officer and Mary Johnston Evans, a member of Delta's board since 1983, will serve as acting non-executive chairman.
ValuJet said it had an operating loss of $9.9 million in the second quarter, as revenues dipped to $47.8 million from $81.2 million a year earlier.
ValuJet, which agreed on July 10 to merge with AirWays Corp. in a deal that would blot out the tarnished ValuJet name, lost $9.6 million, or 18 cents a share, in the 1996 quarter.
"ValuJet continues to make fundamental progress in its plan to return the airline to consistent levels of profitability," ValuJet President D. Joseph Corr said.
During the quarter, ValuJet, also based in Atlanta, resumed service to Dallas/Fort Worth and initiated non-stop jet service between Atlanta and Flint, Mich.

Southwest, based in Dallas, said it benefitted from lower engine repair costs, lower jet fuel prices and cost cutting. The company earned $83.3 million, or 56 cents a share, in the 1996 quarter. Sales rose to $957 million from $910 million.
On Wednesday, Trans World Airlines Inc. posted a big loss for the second quarter, while both US Airways Group Inc. and Continental Airlines Inc. did better than Wall Street had expected.
The results lagged those of the parent companies of United Airlines, the nation's largest carrier, and No. 2 American Airlines, both of which reported better-than-expected results for the quarter.
